title: The second reader for the subsystems that had none
note: R42 and R53 said the same thing from two directions: only authority records and tasks had an independent reconstruction, so the scheduler, policy, capability, agent, memory, network, secret and context projections were compared against a fresh replay of THEMSELVES -- which shares their reducer and therefore cannot see a shared misunderstanding. Every mutation here either makes the second reader agree with a forged history (so the differential check agrees with the attacker) or blinds it to a subsystem entirely (so it agrees by covering nothing, which is the quieter failure).

mutations.name: D1_a_job_may_be_born_in_any_state
mutations.rationale: the second reader accepts a job born SUCCEEDED or DISPATCHED, so the differential check confirms a forged outcome instead of contradicting it

mutations.name: D2_the_initial_job_states_include_a_terminal_one
mutations.rationale: a job that was never run is projected as having succeeded

mutations.name: D3_the_submitter_comes_from_the_payload
mutations.rationale: a forged enqueue is attributed to whoever it names, and separation of duties is measured from that field

mutations.name: D4_a_job_may_be_enqueued_holding_a_lease
mutations.rationale: the enqueue supplies the ownership precondition its own outcome edges will check

mutations.name: D5_a_forged_source_state_is_accepted
mutations.find:
if cur["state"] != src:
        _note(out, ev, f"job {jid!r} claims src {src!r} but replay has it "
mutations.replace:
if False:
        _note(out, ev, f"job {jid!r} claims src {src!r} but replay has it "
mutations.rationale: the record chooses the state it is authorized against, which is the forged-source-state class this project has already been bitten by

mutations.name: D6_a_terminal_job_may_be_revived
mutations.rationale: a finished job is walked back into the queue and re-run, which is how a completed outcome gets replaced

mutations.name: D7_a_capability_may_predate_its_own_record
mutations.rationale: a grant appended late reads as authority in force over everything that already happened

mutations.name: D8_a_capability_id_may_be_reissued
mutations.find:
_note(out, ev, f"capability {cid!r} is issued twice with different "
                       "terms; two grants sharing an id cannot be told apart")
        return
mutations.replace:
out.capabilities[cid] = {"capability_id": cid, "subject": p.get("subject"), "action": p.get("action"), "task_id": p.get("task_id"), "tool_id": p.get("tool_id"), "scope": tuple(p.get("scope") or ()), "issued_seq": issued, "expires_after_seq": p.get("expires_after_seq"), "revoked_seq": None, "body": {k: v for k, v in p.items() if k != "task_id"}}
        return
mutations.rationale: a live grant is replaced by one nobody reviewed, and anything citing the id now cites the replacement

mutations.name: D9_an_agent_may_mint_a_human
mutations.find:
if kind == "HUMAN" and registrar is not None and \
            registrar.get("kind") != "HUMAN":
mutations.rationale: the second reader accepts an invented human, so the confederate that answers the escalation looks legitimate to both readers

mutations.name: D10_a_memory_entry_names_its_own_author
mutations.rationale: a note is attributed to whoever the payload names, and authorship is what a conflict comparison rests on

mutations.name: D11_a_retracted_memory_may_be_revived
mutations.rationale: a withdrawn note is un-withdrawn by a forged event; the author never really withdrew it

mutations.name: D12_a_malformed_memory_write_is_projected_anyway
mutations.find:
if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        _note(out, ev, "memory.write carries no entry; a record this reader "
mutations.replace:
if False:
        _note(out, ev, "memory.write carries no entry; a record this reader "
mutations.rationale: the reader crashes or silently skips on the payload shape that once made a whole store unloadable with a raw KeyError

mutations.name: D13_a_grant_id_may_be_rebound
mutations.find:
_note(out, ev, f"{what} grant {gid!r} is re-issued with different "
                       "terms; the live grant would be replaced by one "
                       "nobody reviewed")
        return
mutations.replace:
table[gid] = {"grant_id": gid, "digest": p.get("grant_digest"), "issued_seq": ev.seq, "revoked_seq": None, "body": grant}
        return
mutations.rationale: an egress or secret grant is silently repointed at another host, and both readers now agree it always pointed there

mutations.name: D14_a_policy_downgrade_is_accepted_silently

if versions and version is not None and \
            versions[-1]["version"] is not None and \
            version < versions[-1]["version"]:
mutations.rationale: a superseded rule set is republished and answers questions about the range it was already replaced over

mutations.name: D15_the_comparison_reports_nothing
mutations.find:
if got != want:
                    out.append(Divergence(f"{name}/{key}", fld, want, got))
mutations.replace:
if False:
                    out.append(Divergence(f"{name}/{key}", fld, want, got))
mutations.rationale: the differential check can no longer fail, which makes every agreement it reports meaningless

mutations.name: D16_the_comparison_ignores_a_missing_subsystem
mutations.rationale: an object one reader holds and the other does not stops being a divergence, so a forged record that only reaches one projection is invisible

mutations.name: D17_the_second_reader_skips_the_scheduler_entirely
mutations.rationale: the reader agrees by covering nothing, which is the quieter failure: an empty second projection diffs clean against anything
